name: Plant Classification & Identification

objectives.text: Sort plants into groups such as trees, shrubs, grasses, and flowering plants using features you can see
Identify common local crops, garden plants, and weeds by their common names
Group plants by how people use them, such as food, fiber, feed, lumber, and ornamental plants
Compare monocot and dicot plants using leaf venation, root system, flower parts, and seed characteristics
Classify plants as annuals, biennials, or perennials based on their life cycle
Describe a leaf using correct terms for shape, arrangement, margin, and venation
Classify plants using a dichotomous key based on leaf shape, arrangement, and margin
Identify common local plants that are poisonous to livestock or people or that are invasive in the region
Explain the major divisions of the plant kingdom, including nonvascular plants, ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms
Explain the binomial nomenclature system and classify a plant by genus and species
Evaluate the accuracy of a plant identification app or field guide by checking its result against a dichotomous key and diagnostic features
Identify agricultural and horticultural plants at seedling and mature stages by common and scientific names, as in an FFA plant identification contest
Classify agricultural and herbaceous plants by growth habit, life cycle, cotyledon type, and woody or herbaceous structure
Use leaf morphology features to distinguish between similar species of crops, ornamentals, and weeds
Categorize horticultural plants by purpose, such as floral crops, landscape plants, and foliage or house plants
Create a dichotomous key for a set of local plant specimens
Identify common crop and weed seeds by size, shape, color, and surface features, as in an FFA agronomy contest
Analyze plant family characteristics, such as those of Poaceae, Fabaceae, and Solanaceae, to identify unknown specimens
Prepare a labeled plant collection or herbarium with pressed specimens showing common name, scientific name, family, and collection data
Explain the differences among species, variety, cultivar, and hybrid and how each is shown on seed tags and plant labels
Evaluate why scientific names rather than common names are needed in agricultural and ornamental plant production, trade, and regulation
Justify the placement of a crop or ornamental species within its taxonomic family based on diagnostic structural traits

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, lightly expanding the monocot and dicot comparison and attaching standards at grades 10 and 12. Added competencies that were missing: identifying local plants by common name, grouping by use and by horticultural purpose, life cycle classification, leaf description vocabulary, poisonous and invasive plant identification, major plant kingdom divisions, checking ID apps against keys, FFA contest identification of plants at seedling and mature stages, classification by growth habit, leaf based identification of similar species, building a dichotomous key, crop and weed seed identification, herbarium preparation, species versus cultivar versus hybrid on seed tags, and the importance of scientific names in trade. Left stem vascular anatomy, roots, and hormones to sibling sub-topics.
